text:
laura: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'staged suture' approach for the model-routing / session-proxy surface. Instead of a hard extract, we slip in a thin adapter layer (the 'suture') that lets the new service take ownership piecewise. Goal: lower blast radius, enable per-tenant cutover, and make rollbacks cheap. sketch + questions below.

henry: brief — how much latency are we adding on the hot path?

laura: Expect ~0.5-2ms depending on path (adapter is tiny), we'll measure. Tradeoff: tiny steady overhead vs much safer incremental migration.

maya: I like incremental ownership, but worried about semantic drift while both sides run. How do we validate parity?

laura: plan is layered: 1) response-hash diffing for every routed request (sampled), 2) nightly full-regression on deterministic prompt set, 3) canary traffic with verbose tracing. If diffs appear > threshold, auto-throttle.

henry: Also need to think about KV cache semantics. If new service uses a different cache shape, sutures must normalize keys.

laura: agree — adapter will normalize KV keys and maintain per-tenant namespacing. ops will expose a feature flag to toggle normalization mode.

simon: operational guard: gate total QPS to suture path until perf monitor ok. Recommend quota token bucket per-tenant: start at 1% of tenant qps, ramp by doubling every hour.

laura: sounds good. I'll add a ramp policy section. example rollout snippet: 
```
rollout:
  stage: "suture-enable"
  per_tenant_ramp: { start_fraction: 0.01, doubling_interval_mins: 60, max_fraction: 1.0 }
  monitors: [ "response-hash", "latency-p95", "error-rate" ]
  auto_throttle_on: { "diff_rate>0.5%": "halve_ramp" }
  auto_rollback_on: { "error_rate>1%": "rollback" }
```

maya: +1. Can the monitoring include semantic-aware checks (e.g., downstream intent extraction)? Hash diffs can be noisy.

laura: yes — plan is two-tier: hash diffs for signal, then targeted semantic evals for flagged prompts. We'll feed flagged prompts to eval pipeline.

henry: where do feature flags live? we need a single source-of-truth for per-tenant routing config.

laura: proposal: config-service (existing) store per-tenant flags; runtime pulls via feature-proxy with short TTL. will add cache invalidation hooks.

infra-bot: Created INF-452: "feature-proxy / per-tenant flagging for suture rollouts". Assignee: infra-team. ETA: 48h for spike. Link: https://tracker/redwood/INF-452

simon: also request an observability dash: routes showing percent of traffic on suture vs legacy, diff-rate heatmap, and per-tenant ramp state.

laura: noted. I'll propose dash tiles in the RFC addendum.

maya: lifecycle question — when do we remove sutures? We don't want permanent adapters.

laura: lifecycle policy: after 2 consecutive weeks with <0.1% diffs and >95% traffic routed, mark tenant sutures for auto-prune; change is queued for ops review and can be fast-tracked.

henry: testing — we should add integration test harness that simulates KV mismatch, latency spikes, and rollback triggers.

laura: adding test harness to the spike. I'll draft an addendum with perf test plan, roll-forward/rollback playbook, and upgrade checklist.

simon: +:thumbsup: from me. If infra-ticket lands, we can schedule the spike next week.

maya: agree. small nit — include a migration-id in headers so we can query logs by migration across services.

laura: good call, will add X-Migration-Id header and wire it into tracing.

henry: once you post RFC addendum, I'll sign off on perf portion.

laura: will post addendum EOD today. Thanks all for quick feedback.
